about: The one source of what's new, per version. The app bundles this file for its once-per-upgrade sheet (packages/swift/WhatsNewKit), and `store` is the text a store's What's New field takes. Every line must be true of the build it ships in, written from git history. No real player, team, league or broadcaster names, no logos or marks, no real people, politics or tragedy. tests/test_whats_new.py enforces what it can. A card may carry a `destination` (one of WhatsNewDestination's cases in Sources/WhatsNew.swift: `lastWeek`, `game`); it becomes a 'Show me' callout that closes the sheet and opens that place. Leave it out for a change with nowhere to go. To look at it in a debug build without recording a version: launch with `-whatsNewPreview`, add `-whatsNewTap <destination>` to press that callout, `-whatsNewOpenNotes` to unfold the notes.

releases.headline: Keeping score, quietly
releases.subhead: A quiet week on the field. The app now counts how it gets used, and one switch turns that off.

cards.title: The Box Score, Not the Roster
cards.line: The app counts its own use: opened, the stadium entered. Never a league, team or player.

cards.title: Your Call, Coach
cards.line: Rather not? Tap the gear, then turn off Share usage stats. It forgets its id.

cards.title: Still Spoiler-Free
cards.line: Last week's games, each with a reason it's worth an hour. Scores stay hidden until you ask.

notes: Usage counts: the app now sends a few counts - a session started, and which space opened (the board, the immersive board, the tabletop or the stadium) - with a random id made on this device, to our own relay at mutaafaziz.com.
Never sent: your leagues, teams, players, the board's address, a video URL, anything you type, your location or an advertising id. The board on your Mac is never told about any of this.
To stop them, open Where is the board?, then Privacy, and turn off Share usage stats. That deletes the id and anything not yet sent.
releases.store: Keeping score, quietly. The app now counts how it is used - a session, and which space opened - with a random id made on the device and nothing about your leagues. Turn it off any time: Where is the board?, Privacy, Share usage stats.

releases.headline: Previously, on Sunday...
releases.subhead: The trade window slammed shut on November 10. These four moves never needed a counter-offer.

cards.title: Instant Replay, All Day
cards.line: Missed a Sunday? The whip-around channel can now replay a finished day, every game at once.

cards.title: Spoiler Alert: None
cards.line: Last week's games, each with a reason it's worth an hour. Final scores stay hidden until you ask.

cards.title: The Ball Is the Main Character
cards.line: Runs stay on the grass, passes drop back and throw, kicks hang - the way the play-by-play tells it.

cards.title: Hold the Confetti
cards.line: Banners, fireworks and the crowd now wait for the ball to land before they celebrate.

notes: Replay a whole finished day: the slate is rebuilt from each play's own timestamp, so the whip-around channel moves between games just as it did live.
Last week's games: pick one by its reason to watch - lead changes, overtime, a late winning score, a comeback. Final scores stay hidden until you turn Scores on.
Every play gets its own path: runs on the grass, passes that drop and throw, punts and kicks with real hang time. No players are drawn; the feed has no tracking data.
Touchdown and field goal celebrations hold until the ball lands, and the board's words and its score now change on the same frame.
The boards along the stadium wall carry the game: both scores, the clock, the down and distance.
The home club's colours now paint both end zones. Visitors keep their own stands and bench.
The crowd faces the field from every seat.
Tap Controls, or pinch anywhere in the stadium, to bring the panels to where you're facing.
When the board's server has a problem, the app now shows the server's own explanation instead of blaming your network.
releases.store: Previously, on Sunday... Replay a whole finished day on the whip-around channel. Pick last week's games by why they're worth watching, with final scores hidden until you ask. Every play now flies its own path, and celebrations wait for the ball to land. Plus: game boards along the stadium wall, home colours in both end zones, and clearer messages when the board's server has a problem.
